metadata.generator: text-to-robot design engine (real components + printed structure)
notes: Interpreted locally: type inferred, DOF=14, gripper=parallel.
metadata.source_prompt: Build WALL-E: a tracked trash-compactor robot with a telescoping neck, binocular eyes and two gripper arms

design.summary: Arduino WALL-E: TPU tracks on 4 TT motors, pan/tilt binocular head, two-joint arms with gripping hands, 1.17 kg, $100 of parts

uses: plug-in wiring: Nano + the front TB6612FNG
LM2596 set to 5.0 V for the neck and hand servos
LM2596 set to 5.0 V for the shoulder and elbow servos
rail splices, the star ground and bus hubs

assumptions: Joint limits trimmed to the collision-free range found by exact solid sweeps: left_arm_lift [-1.00, 1.00] -> [-1.00, 0.49]; right_arm_lift [-1.00, 1.00] -> [-0.49, 1.00]; left_elbow [-1.50, 1.50] -> [-1.50, 1.25]; right_elbow [-1.50, 1.50] -> [-1.25, 1.50]; left_hand [-0.60, 0.60] -> [-0.01, 0.60]; right_hand [-0.60, 0.60] -> [-0.60, 0.01].
tracks print in TPU 95A (flexible), everything else in PETG/PLA+; the body prints open side up without supports
TT motor continuous torque taken as 30 % of the 0.8 kg.cm stall; a turn on the spot is a short transient above that (the tracks slide sideways), so spin in bursts on carpet or rubber floors
prices are typical single-unit marketplace prices and vary by seller
